uncertain: what conclusions geometry or simplified model data warrant
learner_preset.measurement_warning: No mastery percentages or independently measured learner outcomes are inferred.

hardest_target.subconcept: Execute a supplied orbital-overlap model without extrapolating its functional form to total molecular energy.
hardest_target.X: If the overlap factor is cos(theta), total molecular energy must also be cos(theta).
hardest_target.Y: Separate a model variable from a system quantity and identify the extra relation/evidence needed to connect them.
hardest_target.Z: Angle-slider interaction: predict cos(theta) at 0, 60, 90 degrees; then judge competing total-energy claims while a second case keeps theta fixed but changes a non-overlap energy contribution.
hardest_target.W: cos(theta) is warranted only for the supplied overlap factor; values 1, 1/2 and 0 follow at 0, 60 and 90 degrees, but no total-energy dependence follows without an additional energetic model/evidence.

questions.label: Q1
questions.capability: Choose a local orbital model for amide nitrogen that coordinates sigma framework with p-like lone-pair donation, and state the model's limits.
questions.solution_summary: Use an approximately sp2/trigonal-planar sigma-framework description with a p-like lone-pair donor orbital aligned to the carbonyl pi system; reject automatic four-domains-therefore-sp3 as sufficient. Treat sp2 as a compact model label, not the cause of delocalisation or a unique measured orbital decomposition.
questions.X: Four Lewis domains force an exact sp3 description even when the supplied delocalisation model needs a p-like donor orbital.
questions.Y: Local electron-domain counting is conditional; delocalisation-sensitive orbital alignment can make an automatic local label inadequate.
questions.Z: Compare a four-domain local-count card with an alignment card and require the learner to state which evidence each can and cannot explain.
questions.W: The useful model is approximately sp2-like at N with a p-like lone pair aligned to the carbonyl pi system, but the label is descriptive and non-unique.

questions.label: Q2
questions.capability: Represent planar versus approximately 90-degree-twisted formamide while keeping connectivity and formal electron count invariant.
questions.solution_summary: Draw the same atoms/connectivity and Lewis lone pair in both cases. In the planar model the N donor p-like orbital can align with the carbonyl p system; after ~90-degree C-N torsion the relevant orbital directions are orthogonal/poorly aligned. The sketches are qualitative and do not measure donation strength.
questions.X: Twisting changes the Lewis electron count or connectivity, or the drawing itself measures donation strength.
questions.Y: Separate invariant bookkeeping from changed three-dimensional orbital orientation.
questions.Z: Linked before/after orbital sketch with a fixed connectivity/electron-count strip and a rotatable donor-orbital overlay.
questions.W: Rotation changes alignment while formal electron count and atom connectivity remain the same; qualitative sketches do not quantify donation.

questions.label: Q3
questions.capability: Explain the supplied twisting result through overlap and distinguish model assumptions from measured facts.
questions.solution_summary: Twisting reduces compatible N-to-carbonyl orbital overlap in the supplied model, so a delocalisation contribution tied to that interaction is reduced. 'The hybridisation label changes' is not a sufficient cause; exact donation and energetics require a specified model or measurement.
questions.X: Hybridisation label change itself causes donation to disappear.
questions.Y: Use orbital geometry/interaction as the model mechanism and keep exact energetic claims evidence-bound.
questions.Z: Cause-sort interaction: label, geometry, overlap, donation and measurement cards must be placed in warranted causal/evidential order.
questions.W: Reduced aligned overlap supports reduced delocalisation in the supplied model; the label is shorthand, and exact energetic magnitude is not established by the prompt.

questions.label: Q4
questions.capability: Decide whether lone-pair conjugation is plausible by combining local count, adjacency, continuous orbital pathway, alignment and model validity.
questions.solution_summary: Site A has the supplied amide donor/adjacent carbonyl pathway; site B is interrupted by saturated CH2 in the simplified model. Spatial proximity alone is insufficient. A structural change that creates an unsaturated/appropriately aligned continuous orbital path requires reassessment.
questions.X: Any nearby lone pair and carbonyl are conjugated.
questions.Y: Conjugation requires a structurally continuous compatible orbital pathway, not closeness alone.
questions.Z: Pathway checker: learner traces local count -> adjacency -> continuous p path -> alignment -> model-validity checkpoints for A, B and a counterfactual.
questions.W: A passes the supplied pathway test; B fails at the saturated CH2 interruption; changing the bridge/connectivity can invalidate the original decision.

questions.label: Q5
questions.capability: Replace an over-strong hybridisation/bond-angle claim with a qualified model claim and identify evidence needed for stronger physical conclusions.
questions.solution_summary: Hybridisation/domain labels are first-order local models, not unique angle predictors. CH4, NH3 and H2O can share introductory four-domain/sp3-type language while lone-pair occupancy changes molecular geometry and angles. Amide N shows an additional delocalisation-sensitive boundary. Geometry constrains models but does not uniquely prove an orbital decomposition.
questions.X: One hybridisation label uniquely fixes one bond angle, so any deviation disproves the label.
questions.Y: Separate electron-domain classification from exact geometry and from unique electronic-structure claims.
questions.Z: Claim stress-test matrix across CH4/NH3/H2O/formamide with columns for what the local model predicts and what it does not.
questions.W: The label is a useful first-order descriptor whose quantitative/unique explanatory scope is limited; stronger claims need additional structural, spectroscopic or computational evidence.

questions.label: Q6
questions.capability: Distinguish knowing the four-domain rule from deciding when its localised assumptions are adequate.
questions.solution_summary: Use four-domain counting for a first local classification when bonding is sufficiently localised and no supplied evidence requires a conjugation-sensitive model. Automatic use becomes inadequate when resonance-sensitive planarity, aligned donor/acceptor orbitals, radical/SOMO character or structural change matters.
questions.X: A memorised counting rule is automatically applicable whenever four domains are drawn.
questions.Y: Applicability conditions are a separate reasoning step from recall.
questions.Z: Rule-or-evidence gate: choose whether to stop at local counting or escalate to orbital-pathway analysis.
questions.W: Local counting is conditional; Site A needs the delocalisation-sensitive model, while Site B can be treated more locally under the supplied simplified assumptions.

questions.label: Q7
questions.capability: Translate the supplied planar methyl-radical model without turning it into a universal three-sigma-bond rule.
questions.solution_summary: Represent three coplanar C-H sigma directions and a singly occupied p-like orbital perpendicular to the plane. The proposed universal statement fails because the orbital is not empty and the supplied CH3 radical model does not prove a theorem about every three-coordinate center.
questions.X: Three sigma bonds always leave an empty p orbital.
questions.Y: Track occupancy explicitly and distinguish one supplied case from a universal rule.
questions.Z: Orbital occupancy sketch: empty, singly occupied and doubly occupied p-like options; learner selects the one warranted by CH3· and labels the scope.
questions.W: The p-like orbital is singly occupied in the supplied model; no universal empty-p conclusion follows.

questions.label: Q8
questions.capability: Propose observations that discriminate localised versus delocalised amide descriptions while separating consistency from unique proof.
questions.solution_summary: Useful evidence includes planarity/pyramidality, C-N structural/rotational behavior, spectroscopy and defined electronic-structure calculations. Planarity can support consistency with conjugation but cannot by itself quantify donation or uniquely establish one electronic partition/model.
questions.X: If nitrogen is planar, resonance magnitude and the unique orbital description have been proved.
questions.Y: Evidence can discriminate predictions while remaining non-unique with respect to causal/electronic models.
questions.Z: Evidence-to-claim matching: drag geometry, rotation, spectroscopy and calculation onto claims they warrant; reject overclaims.
questions.W: Geometry is useful discriminating evidence but alone cannot quantify donation or prove a unique electronic-structure account.

questions.label: Q9
questions.capability: Execute the supplied cos(theta) overlap model and reject an unsupported transfer of that functional form to total molecular energy.
questions.solution_summary: cos(0)=1, cos(60)=1/2, cos(90)=0 for the supplied overlap factor. This does not imply total molecular energy varies as cos(theta): total energy has other contributions and any energetic dependence on overlap requires its own explicit relation/model/evidence.
questions.X: The overlap factor and total molecular energy must have the same cos(theta) functional dependence.
questions.Y: Keep the scope of a supplied mathematical relation attached to its defined quantity.
questions.Z: Angle slider with live overlap gauge plus claim-choice panel; a second fixed-theta case varies a non-overlap energy contribution to expose underdetermination.
questions.W: Only the overlap-factor values 1, 1/2 and 0 are warranted; the total-energy law is unspecified.

questions.label: Q10
questions.capability: Build a qualified decision framework for when local hybridisation counting is useful and when extra orbital/evidence models are needed.
questions.solution_summary: Use local sigma/lone-pair inventory first, then test connectivity/adjacency, compatible p/SOMO/donor-acceptor pathways, and model sufficiency before using a hybridisation label at the warranted descriptive level. NH3 exposes lone-pair geometry effects; allene requires orthogonal p systems; formamide is delocalisation-sensitive; the separated amine lacks the supplied continuous path.
questions.X: One count-and-label rule explains every shape and reactivity difference.
questions.Y: Turn the shortcut into a staged model-selection framework with escalation criteria.
questions.Z: Four-case decision tree learner must traverse, with an evidence-escalation branch for claims beyond the local model.
questions.W: Local counting is useful but conditional; stronger electronic/reactivity claims require an appropriate orbital model and/or independent evidence.

findings.detail: A stale pre-v2 question set was initially used for one issue-comment draft. Live Issue #37 was re-read; comment 5977895785 was replaced in place with v2 analysis before this ledger was committed. No stale academic records existed on the candidate branch.

Issue requires the supplied benchmark questions preserved in Core2 while the generic Core2 role normally reserves Core2 for teacher-original/approved source custody. The candidate will preserve wording and coordinator/AI authorship and record the discrepancy rather than invent exam provenance.
